frozen: DRAFT: not frozen. The circuit digest and the threshold arm's hunger point are filled in from the clean-commit cut and its calibration before the held-out split runs.
question: Can a circuit cut from the FlyWire v783 whole brain decide when a mortal research fly feeds, for a whole 8-hour life in the ecology, without leaving it worse fed than the deployed controller leaves it; does its wiring matter; and does it cost little enough to run in the loop?
status: A seeded study on disposable research subjects, not a registered R.A.I.N. experiment. No subject is Eva or ECHO, a copy or a continuation; nothing here reaches them.

circuit.made_by: python -m fly_neural reduce cut (fly-neural/experiments/feeding-reduced-v783.json), from the pinned FlyWire v783 release; kept outside the repository

feeding.notes: Sugar GRNs at max_rate_hz x hunger while on food (Inagaki et al. 2012: starvation raises sugar-GRN sensitivity; the linear form and the 200 Hz ceiling, twice Shiu et al.'s standard 100 Hz stimulus, are this model's). threshold_hz is fly-neural's own feed readout (mean MN9 rate >= 10 Hz); window_ms is the trailing window the neural shadow's food result called for. hunger_at, for the threshold arm only, is where the intact circuit's readout first reaches threshold_hz (calibrate).
feeding.calibration: connectome-feeding-evaluate.ts calibrate on this circuit: 40 trials of 1 s per input rate from 10 Hz in steps of 2 Hz; the readout (500 ms) first reaches 10 Hz at 46 Hz input, hunger 46/200 = 0.23.

body: Mortal, with the thirst policy and without the heat policy (Stage B found the heat policy raised heat exposure).

arms.controller: The deployed controller decides feeding, as it does now (with the thirst policy over it).
arms.connectome: The reduced FAFB v783 circuit's MN9 readout decides feeding; the controller does everything else. Primary arm.
arms.shuffled: The same circuit with its weights shuffled across its synapse pairs (seeded per fly): the same numbers, the wiring lost.
arms.threshold: Feeding while on food whenever hunger >= hunger_at: the intact circuit reduced to the one number where its readout crosses threshold.

endpoints: Time-weighted mean reserve over the life (sampled each minute while alive); fed energy (J); alive at the horizon and cause of death; feeding seconds and bouts; the hybrid's meals and vetoes; the circuit's wall time.

bootstrap.rule: Paired percentile bootstrap over environments (every fly and arm of a drawn environment kept); 95% interval.

criteria.rule: Held-out: the interval of mean reserve(connectome) - (1 - margin) x mean reserve(controller) excludes 0 (above): the connectome leaves the fly no worse fed than the controller, within 20%.
Held-out: the interval of mean reserve(connectome) - mean reserve(shuffled) excludes 0 (above): the wiring, not the numbers, does it.
Held-out: no more connectome flies than controller flies die of starvation.

Held-out: on food the circuit runs at least 10 times faster than real time on the machine that ran it: its wall time over the connectome runs, divided by the simulated seconds its sugar neurons were driven, is at most max_circuit_s_per_driven_s. Its share of the runs' total wall time is reported.
